narrative: Routine, low-frequency contact over roughly seven months — API scope questions, an ERP-migration feature request, dashboard versioning and report-builder scripting queries. Every ticket is a how-to or feature ask, all resolved within a week, with no complaints or repeat issues anywhere in the thread. This reads as a healthy, moderately engaged account with no risk signal in the text.

Frequent complaints across nearly every module (connectors, seats, dashboards, alerts, API, report builder) recur over 16 months, often explicitly flagged as repeats — "same as last quarter", "similar to what happened in May". Every ticket resolves in one or two days and the customer twice notes fixes "usually get sorted quickly once someone looks at it", pointing to a demanding but engaged user rather than one heading for the door. Still, a new module breaking almost every month for over a year, with the dashboard and alert threads left hanging at the end, is a real product-quality signal worth monitoring.

Connector sync failures recurred three times (Aug 2024, Jan and May 2025) with the customer stating outright "we were told this was fixed — clearly it wasn't", escalating in May to looping in their CSM and warning of "a serious conversation about the contract". That escalation produced a real turnaround: by July 2025 the customer writes "good to actually see this resolved properly for once", and the following two months are calm, low-stakes tickets — a seat audit, a new Xero connector, minor PDF formatting. This is a recovered account, with only a trivial alert-digest-timing issue left open.
Single onboarding ticket (NetSuite OAuth setup), resolved in two days. Not enough history to indicate any risk beyond a normal setup question.

Ten urgent tickets across eight months (Feb–Oct 2024), all resolved within a day or two, but the customer repeatedly flags recurrence — alerts going silent "same pattern as February", connectors failing for "the third connector issue since May". The history stops abruptly after the October cluster with no ticket confirming the underlying instability was ever addressed, unlike accounts that end on an explicit "this has held" note. Chronic multi-module failures ending on live, unresolved-feeling frustration is a concerning pattern.

Chronic, recurring bugs concentrated in report builder (four separate incidents Feb–Oct 2025: lost formatting, crashes, reset colours, freezing) and exports (three incidents), each fixed quickly but never with a confirming follow-up. By June the customer is visibly fatigued — "reported similar issues before, this is getting old" — and the most recent ticket (Oct 2025) is still a raw complaint about report builder freezing, with no calming signal anywhere in the account's history.

A steady stream of feature requests and positive feedback — Slack routing for alerts, historical API snapshots, praise for a cross-filter feature that "cut our monthly close reporting time significantly" — with only trivial bugs mentioned in passing. The customer offers to be a design partner on the API roadmap. Engaged, expanding account with no risk signal in the text.
Six routine how-to and configuration questions spread over nine months, all resolved without complaint. Healthy, low-touch account.
Single ticket about report templates missing after an account migration, resolved in eight days. A one-off data-continuity scare with no further pattern to judge risk from.
Four routine configuration questions over seven months, no complaints, all resolved. Healthy account.

Six low-key how-to and minor-annoyance tickets (filter resets, dashboard sharing, bulk import) over five months, calm tone throughout — "not urgent", "a bit annoying" — all resolved. Healthy, engaged account.

Six technical API questions over more than a year as the customer builds out an integration (auth method, versioning, sandbox environment). No complaints, all resolved — a healthy, technically engaged account.

A chronic run of failures from Nov 2024 through March 2025 (connector, alerts, exports, API, report builder) brought visibly rising frustration — "starting to lose confidence that a fix stays fixed" — then an explicit escalation demanding "a call this week" in March. That report-builder issue was never formally closed out; an August ticket admits it was "worked around manually the whole spring". Everything since — dashboards, API, exports — is confirmed fixed and holding, with the customer twice thanking the team for a fix "actually holding this time". Net trajectory is a genuine recovery, with one unconfirmed thread lingering underneath.
Three routine questions from a single named contact over two months, all resolved without complaint. Healthy account.

A single fault — report-builder formulas wiping on refresh — recurred on and off for ten months (Dec 2024 to Sept 2025) despite being marked fixed twice, with the customer noting "a fixed issue keeps coming back"; a separate seat-provisioning problem took 30 days and three tickets to resolve, prompting an explicit request for "someone senior". By October both threads are confirmed durably fixed — "hasn't recurred once, including through two refresh cycles" — and the account ends on calm, low-stakes feature requests. A hard-won recovery, though the budget-variance alert complaint from May was never followed up and remains open.

Report-builder formula errors recurred for ten months (Dec 2024–Oct 2025, explicitly the "third ticket on this" by January) and dashboards went down during board week in April, triggering an explicit escalation request. Both threads are since confirmed resolved — dashboards "held through two board cycles", formulas "several months clean" as of October — and the account ends on calm, minor feature requests. A genuine, if slow, recovery with nothing left unresolved in the text.

A cluster of overlapping issues in mid-2024 — a date filter that wouldn't lock, intermittent API 401s, and alert emails that stopped sending — with the customer noting "I've logged this three times" on the API issue. All three are confirmed resolved by 19 July, and the only ticket since (September) is a calm documentation question. Recovered account, low residual risk.

Dense, wide-ranging technical friction over four months (API pagination bugs, an undocumented breaking field-name change, export timeouts, spam-filtered alerts) on a heavily API-integrated account. Most damaging: a connector SSL failure on their "primary data source", first raised as unresolved in November, still "nothing back from support" days later, referenced again in December as "still broken too" — then never mentioned again or confirmed fixed. Combined with "before we build anything on top of this we need to know the documentation is reliable", this reads as an engineering team's trust in the platform eroding around a business-critical issue that appears to have simply dropped off rather than been resolved.
Seven varied feature and configuration questions over a year (comparison periods, SSO, SFTP delivery, alert cooldowns), calm tone throughout, all resolved. Healthy, steadily engaged account.
Three routine admin and API questions over four months, no complaints, all resolved. Healthy, low-touch account.
